thesis: Jesse Livermore defines an upside-down market as one where the normal correlation between economic strength and stock market performance is inverted, causing good economic news to be bad for stocks and bad economic news to be good. He argues that while monetary policy has limited stimulative effects that can be offset by weak organic growth, fiscal policy is powerful enough to achieve any nominal growth outcome, making an economy needing fiscal stimulus potentially bullish because it receives both the stimulus and the accompanying monetary stimulus.
